title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is shared by every instance on the machine; a second instance is offered another run's live sequence and cannot dismiss the prompt
what_happened: My sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning/data; DB had 0 sequences, 0 sequence_runs, 0 sequence_checkpoints, 0 captured_images) put up a modal "Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. Sequence: New Sequence, Saved: 2m ago, Completed: 6 frames (0m integration)". The log line was 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' — the shared user support dir, not the configured data dir. That file (skotiq_session.checkpoint, mtime advancing every few seconds, containing a 20x3s "Take Exposures" node I never created) belongs to a different Skotiq process running concurrently. Clicking "Discard" three times did not dismiss the dialog — the other process rewrote the checkpoint within ~3s each time, so the app re-detected it and re-prompted, leaving the GUI wedged behind a modal barrier (barrierDismissible:false, Escape ignored). I had to relaunch with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected to escape it.
expected: The checkpoint must live under the instance's own data root (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / the profile's directory), so two Skotiq processes on one machine — the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing, or two profiles — never see each other's run. "Resume" here would have loaded and started a sequence belonging to another rig.
repro: 1. Run two Skotiq desktop instances on one machine with different SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR. 2. Start a sequence in instance A. 3. Launch/relaunch instance B -> "Recover Sequence?" appears in B describing A's run. 4. Click Discard repeatedly while A is still checkpointing -> dialog reappears each time.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-77-plan-nofw.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-81-discarded.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-82-discard2.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-83-discard3.png; /tmp/ns-audit/planning/app.log line 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop'; head of /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint
proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint directory the same way the DB path is resolved — honour SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR (and the headless code's `<support>/checkpoints` sub-directory convention from apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-33) instead of the bare application-support root. Additionally, after a Discard that is immediately followed by a fresh checkpoint from another writer, do not silently re-prompt in a loop: record the discarded checkpoint id/timestamp and suppress it, and give the dialog a "Not now" escape.
verdict_reasoning: Core path bug CONFIRMED: my own sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/data) logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/app.log), i.e. the shared per-app support root, not the configured data dir. Source confirms: app_shell.dart:342-348 passes the bare getApplicationSupportDirectory() to backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir. Dialog details confirmed too (app_shell.dart:373 barrierDismissible:false; only 'Discard'/'Resume' actions at :450-464; no 'Not now'). TWO SUPPORTING CLAIMS REFUTED. (1) 'the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing' would collide: it would not. The headless host resolves <support>/checkpoints (apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-18) while the GUI uses the <support> root, so they write different files; on disk today only .../com.skotiq.desktop/checkpoints/skotiq_session.checkpoint exists. Only two GUI instances collide. (2) 'Discard three times did not dismiss the dialog because the other process rewrote the checkpoint and the app re-prompted': runAppCheckpointRecovery (app_shell.dart:60-83) loops ONLY when resume()/discard() throws; a successful discard returns AppStartupCheckpointOutcome.discarded and exits. Re-prompting therefore requires backend.discardCheckpoint to throw, which the finding does not establish and I could not reproduce. SEVERITY corrected P1 -> P3: production installs are one-instance-per-data-dir (the app takes a per-data-dir single-instance lock), so the blast radius is the audit harness / a deliberately multi-profile user, not a shipping rig.

title: A rig with no filter wheel cannot create any integration goal, so the autopilot can never be given a target
what_happened: With the saved profile 'My First Rig' (sim camera + sim mount, filter wheel deliberately skipped — the normal OSC/DSLR/mono-without-wheel case), opening a queue row's target editor shows the Integration goals section with the message 'Equipment profile has no filters configured; configure a filter wheel first.' and NO 'Add goal' control of any kind. Since the scheduler's own empty state states 'The scheduler needs targets with integration goals', a wheel-less rig can never populate the Target queue and the Unattended Autopilot is unusable. (I could only exercise the editor at all by inserting an integration_goals row directly into the scratch DB.)
expected: A profile with no filter wheel should be able to set a single unfiltered goal. The Smart Night builder already handles exactly this case — packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_night_service.dart:80-98 comments 'An empty filter list is the normal state of an OSC rig with no wheel — Smart Night plans a single unfiltered row for it' — so the scheduler and the sequence builder disagree about whether wheel-less rigs are supported.
repro: 1. Onboarding: skip the Filter wheel step, save the profile. 2. Plan Tonight > Schedule > click a queued target row (needs a target in the active project) -> Integration goals section. 3. Observe the warning and the absence of any add-goal affordance.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/scheduler/widgets/integration_goals_editor.dart (the add-goal control is gated on a non-empty filter list); mirrored in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:551-560 (_availableFilters returns profile.filterNames)
proposed_fix: When the active profile has no filter wheel, offer a single synthetic unfiltered goal slot (label it 'No filter', matching the chip the Recommendation card already renders) instead of blocking the editor, and stop treating an empty filter list as a mis-configuration. Keep the hard error only for the real fault the Smart Night builder already distinguishes: a wheel that IS connected but reports zero slots.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced in the UI. With 'My First Rig' (sim camera + sim mount, filter-wheel step skipped) I seeded three catalog targets and one goal each, re-evaluated, and opened the M92 queue row: the Integration goals section renders the existing goal plus the amber line 'Equipment profile has no filters configured; configure a filter wheel first.' and no add-goal affordance whatsoever (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-60-rowclick.png). Source confirms: integration_goals_editor.dart:588 returns only that Text when widget.availableFilters.isEmpty, short-circuiting the whole _AddGoalRow; availableFilters ultimately comes from SchedulerCandidateLoader._availableFilters (scheduler_provider.dart:551-560), which returns profile.filterNames and is empty for a wheel-less profile. IntegrationGoalsEditor is the ONLY goal editor in the app (used at target_editor_overlay.dart:101 and projects_tab_content.dart:483), so a wheel-less rig has no path to create a goal, and the scheduler empty state does demand 'targets with integration goals'. CITATION CORRECTION: the 'An empty filter list is the normal state of an OSC rig with no wheel' comment cited as smart_night_service.dart:80-98 is actually at packages/skotiq_app/lib/utils/plan_tonight_sequencer_helper.dart:85-98 (smart_night_service.dart:80-98 is the meridian-flip/weather-recovery predicates). The substance - that the Smart Night path deliberately supports wheel-less rigs while the scheduler blocks them - holds. P2 stands.

title: False "Rises late" warning on a target that is up all night, and the same card gives two different rise times
what_happened: The Night Outlook hero card for M92 shows the warning '⚠ Rises late at 11:54' while the chart footer of the same card shows 'Rise: 12:01  Transit: 21:34  Set: 07:06' and the chips say 'Peak in dark 84.0°, 5.3h visible'. Two problems on one card: (a) the warning is false — at astronomical dark (22:01) M92 is already above 80°, it is up for the entire imaging window; (b) the warning's rise time (11:54) and the footer's rise time (12:01) disagree by 7 minutes for the same event.
expected: No 'rises late' warning for a target that clears the minimum altitude at the start of astronomical darkness. And one rise time per card.
repro: Site 40/-75, Plan Tonight > Recommendation, hero card = M92 (top-scored on 2026-08-01), scroll to the warning rows under the chips.
where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/planning/target_scoring.dart:1006-1024 (warning compares visibility.riseTime against nightStart with no check that the rise is in daylight / on the correct day)
proposed_fix: Same root cause as the P0 window bug: visibility.riseTime comes from the noon-anchored calculateObjectVisibility and can name a rise on the wrong day or in broad daylight. Gate the warning on the target's actual altitude at nightStart (if alt >= minAltitude at nightStart, there is nothing to warn about) rather than on a rise timestamp, and source both the warning and the footer from the same visibility object.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim once M92 became the optimizer's primary pick (score 77). The Night Outlook hero card shows chips 'Peak in dark 84.0 deg' and '5.3h visible', the warning row 'Rises late at 11:54', and in the same card's chart footer 'Rise: 12:01  Transit: 21:34  Set: 07:06' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-54-hero.png). Both halves hold: the target clears 30 deg before astronomical dark begins at 22:01, and one card prints two rise times 7 minutes apart. Mechanism verified: the warning uses visibility.riseTime from target_scoring.dart:1006-1024 (gated only on riseTime.isAfter(nightStart) and riseOffset > 0.66*nightDuration, with no daylight/wrong-day check), and that visibility is the nightMid-anchored solve; the chart footer comes from a SEPARATE solve inside AltitudeChart, which calls calculateObjectVisibility with date: now (altitude_chart.dart:156-163) and renders Rise/Transit/Set at :627-652. Two different anchor dates for the same event is the source of the 11:54 vs 12:01 split, so the proposed fix's 'source both from the same visibility object' is correct. Shares the noon-anchoring root cause with the P0 finding but is a distinct surface and a distinct code path, so not a duplicate. P2 stands.

title: Observing Alerts refresh is a silent no-op and the screen can never show anything
what_happened: The Observing Alerts screen says 'Real targets for citizen science' and 'Transient alerts from AAVSO, TNS, and other sources will appear here when available.' Clicking the refresh icon produces no spinner, no last-refreshed timestamp, no result count, no error, and no row — before and after, at +3s and +15s, the screen is byte-identical. transient_detections stayed at 0. Enabling TNS (which requires a bot API key that this sheet has no field for) and refreshing again also produced no error. Nothing is written to the app log. Separately, the only implemented broadband source is called at a URL that cannot return anything useful: `https://www.aavso.org/vsx/index.php?view=api.list&format=json&maxrec=50` 301-redirects to vsx.aavso.org and then returns exactly `{"VSXObjects":[]}` (verified by curl). So the surface is permanently empty and the operator has no way to tell 'no transients tonight' from 'this feature is broken'.
expected: Refresh should show it is working (spinner), report what happened ('AAVSO: 0 alerts, TNS: skipped — no API key, checked 11:16'), and fail loud when an enabled source cannot be reached. TransientAlertFetchException already exists for this; nothing surfaces it.
repro: 1. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 2. Click the refresh icon; screenshot at +3s and +15s. 3. Gear > enable TNS > Done > refresh again. 4. `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select count(*) from transient_detections'` -> 0.
proposed_fix: Point AAVSO at https://vsx.aavso.org/ and at a query that actually selects recent alerts (api.list with no selector returns an empty set by design). Add a per-source status strip to the screen header: source name, last fetch time, alert count or error. Surface TransientAlertFetchException in the UI instead of swallowing it, and tell the user when TNS is enabled but unkeyed.
verdict_reasoning: Core CONFIRMED. curl of the exact production endpoint (transient_alert_service.dart:80-81) shows HTTP 301 www.aavso.org -> vsx.aavso.org and a body of exactly {"VSXObjects":[]}, so the only implemented broadband source returns an empty set by construction. In the app I clicked refresh and diffed pixel-for-pixel: the screen body is byte-identical before, at +2 s and at +10 s (PIL ImageChops bbox None over the content region; only the status-bar clock changed), and sqlite3 'select count(*) from transient_detections' stayed 0. No last-refreshed timestamp, no source status, no result count anywhere on the surface, and a partial failure (TNS enabled but unkeyed, transient_alert_service.dart:851-870) is swallowed because AAVSO's empty success keeps the batch from throwing. TWO SUPPORTING CLAIMS CORRECTED: (a) the screen is not stateless about failure - transients_screen.dart:105-109 has both loading: _buildLoadingState() and error: _buildErrorState(), and _buildErrorState at :230-234 prints error.toString(), so a total-failure TransientAlertFetchException WOULD surface; what is missing is per-source status and the partial-failure case. (b) 'Nothing is written to the app log' is a non-observation: that file is the Rust backend log and no Dart logger line ever lands in it, while refreshTransientAlerts does call logger.info at transient_alert_provider.dart:1106-1109. P2 stands on the strength of the dead URL and the undetectable difference between 'no transients tonight' and 'this feature is broken'.

title: Night Outlook hero card freezes its "Alt" and "Airmass" readouts while the list card for the same object keeps updating
what_happened: The hero card for NGC6015 showed 'Alt: 14.7°  Airmass: 3.88' at 10:00:55 and still showed exactly 14.7°/3.88 at 10:17:29, seventeen minutes later. In between, the candidate-list card for the same object showed 'Alt: 15.1° Airmass: 3.79' at 10:09:24. The labels are present tense, so the hero card is stating a stale altitude as the current one.
expected: Both cards should track the same clock, or the hero card should timestamp its values.
repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation. Note the hero card's Alt/Airmass. Wait 15 minutes without leaving the tab. Compare with the same object's card in 'Tonight's candidates'.
proposed_fix: Recompute currentAltitude/airmass for the primary card on the same ticker the candidate list uses, or drop the live readout from the hero and keep only the whole-night figures (peak, transit, window hours) that the section header promises.
verdict_reasoning: Underlying defect CONFIRMED, framing corrected. AltitudeChart computes _currentAltitude/_currentAirmass in _calculateData(), which is called only from initState and from didUpdateWidget when raHours/decDegrees change (altitude_chart.dart:61-72) - there is no timer and no clock provider anywhere in the widget, so the chip labelled present-tense 'Alt:' is frozen at whatever the value was when the widget mounted. Observed consistently with that: the NGC6015 hero card read 'Alt: 21.1 deg  Airmass: 2.76' at 11:46 and still read exactly 21.1/2.76 at 11:53 across tab navigation (pv-29-plan.png vs pv-36-hero.png). CORRECTIONS: (1) the candidate-list card does not 'keep updating' either - it uses the identical AltitudeChart; it only recomputes because scrolling recycles it and re-runs initState, which is what produced the reporter's 14.7 vs 15.1 comparison; (2) the 'where' is wrong - the stale readout lives in screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart, not in _primary_target_card.dart / _recommendation_tab.dart:150-159, and the proposed fix 'recompute on the same ticker the candidate list uses' points at a ticker that does not exist. P3 correct.
